name: Fixed-effect model
variables: T_i = observed effect size of study i; mu = common true effect; e_i = within-study sampling error of study i with variance v_i
notes: One level of sampling, one source of error. The FE figure on p. 88 writes epsilon_i for the error term where eq. (2.2) has e_i. Engine: meta_analysis(yi, vi, model='fixed').

name: Fixed-effect inverse-variance weight
variables: w_i = weight of study i; v_i = within-study variance of T_i (v_i = SE_i^2)
notes: Weights by inverse variance, not sample size (pp. 89, 93). Spreadsheet: E3 = 1/D3. Engine requires every v_i > 0 and finite.

name: Fixed-effect pooled estimate
variables: T_bar = FE weighted mean (combined effect); w_i = 1/v_i; T_i = effect of study i; k = number of studies
notes: Spreadsheet F13 = F9/E9. Reading-scores example: 101.833/256.667 = 0.3968 (p. 91).

name: Variance and standard error of the FE pooled estimate
variables: v_bar = variance of T_bar; w_i = FE weight; SE(T_bar) = standard error of T_bar
notes: Spreadsheet F14 = 1/E9, F15 = SQRT(F14). Example: v_bar = 0.0039, SE = 0.0624 (p. 91).

name: 95% Wald confidence interval of the FE pooled estimate
expression: LL = T_bar - 1.96 * SE(T_bar)   (2.7);   UL = T_bar + 1.96 * SE(T_bar)   (2.8)
variables: LL, UL = lower and upper 95% limits; T_bar = FE pooled estimate; SE(T_bar) = its standard error; 1.96 = standard normal 0.975 quantile
notes: Fixed normal multiplier 1.96 (z interval). Typo in the worked example on p. 91: 'Upper Limit = 0.3968 − 1.96*0.0624 = 0.5191' should have '+'; the result 0.5191 is correct. Engine: ci_method='z' (the default for model='fixed'). The engine uses the exact quantile norm_ppf(0.975) = 1.959964 instead of 1.96 (the reading-scores limits differ by a few 1e-6; identical at 4 decimals).

name: Z statistic for the FE pooled estimate
variables: Z = test statistic for H0: mu = 0; T_bar = FE pooled estimate; SE(T_bar) = its standard error
notes: Spreadsheet F18 = F13/F15. Example: Z = 6.3563 (p. 91).

name: One-tailed p-value from Z
variables: Phi = standard normal cumulative distribution function; Z, Z* = FE and RE test statistics
notes: Valid only if the effect is in the hypothesised (pre-specified) direction. Spreadsheet: =(1-(NORMDIST(ABS(F18),0,1,TRUE))) (F19, M19); in current Excel NORMDIST(x,0,1,TRUE) = NORM.S.DIST(x,TRUE). The engine reports only two-sided p; the one-tailed value is distributions.norm_sf(abs(Z)). RE example p*_1T = 0.0006 (p. 101).

name: Two-tailed p-value from Z
variables: Phi = standard normal cumulative distribution function; Z, Z* = FE and RE test statistics
notes: Normal (not t) reference distribution. Spreadsheet F20/M20 = (1-(NORMDIST(ABS(Z),0,1,TRUE)))*2. FE example p < .0001 (displayed 0.0000); RE example 0.0013 (p. 101). Engine meta_analysis uses this when ci_method='z'.

name: Random-effects model
expression: T_i = theta_i + e_i = mu + epsilon_i + e_i   (3.1)
variables: T_i = observed effect of study i; theta_i = true effect of study i; mu = mean of the true effects; epsilon_i = between-study deviation theta_i - mu with variance tau^2; e_i = within-study error with variance v_i (sigma^2 in the figure)
notes: Two levels of sampling, two sources of error. Notation clash: the figure on p. 95 writes theta_1 = mu + xi_1 and T_1 = theta_1 + epsilon_1 (epsilon = within-study error), whereas eq. (3.1) uses epsilon for between-study and e for within-study error. Engine: meta_analysis(yi, vi, model='random').

name: Cochran's Q (definitional form)
variables: Q = weighted sum of squared deviations; w_i = 1/v_i (FE weight); T_i = effect of study i; T_bar = FE pooled estimate; k = number of studies
notes: Uses FE weights. A large study far from the mean contributes more to Q than a small study at the same distance. Reading-scores example Q = 12.8056 (p. 98).

name: Cochran's Q (computational form)
variables: w_i = 1/v_i; T_i = effect of study i; k = number of studies
notes: Algebraically identical to (3.2). Spreadsheet H13 = G9 - F9^2/E9 with G3 = B3^2*E3. Example: 53.208 - 101.833^2/256.667 = 12.8056 (p. 98). The engine (models.cochran_q) evaluates the definitional form (3.2). It is algebraically identical and avoids the cancellation error the computational form can suffer with large weights.

name: Degrees of freedom of Q
variables: df = degrees of freedom; k = number of studies (effect sizes)
notes: Expected value of Q under homogeneity. Spreadsheet H14 = COUNT(B3:B8) - 1. Example df = 5.

name: Scaling factor C for the moment estimator of tau^2
variables: C = scaling constant; w_i = 1/v_i (FE weights)
notes: Puts tau^2 on the scale of the within-study variances because Q is a weighted sum of squares. Spreadsheet H16 = E9 - H9/E9 with H3 = E3^2. Example C = 256.667 - 15522.222/256.667 = 196.1905. Returned as key 'C' by models.heterogeneity and used inside models.tau2_dl.

name: Between-study variance tau^2 (method of moments / DerSimonian-Laird)
expression: tau^2 = (Q - df) / C if Q > df;  tau^2 = 0 if Q <= df   (3.5)   [spreadsheet: MAX(Q - df, 0) / C]
variables: tau^2 = between-study variance of the true effects; Q = Cochran's Q; df = k - 1; C = scaling factor (3.6)
notes: The source does not name it, but this is the DerSimonian-Laird estimator; CMA output in the screenshots matches it. Truncated at zero. Example tau^2 = 0.0398 (full precision 0.039786; shown as 0.040 in the spreadsheet column, p. 102). [note: later guidance (Veroniki et al. 2016; Cochrane Handbook v6) favours REML or Paule-Mandel; engine default is REML, so pass tau2_method='DL' to reproduce the source.] [note: DL tends to underestimate tau^2 when k is small, and often returns exactly 0.]

name: Random-effects total variance and weight
variables: v_i* = total variance of study i under RE; v_i = within-study variance; tau^2 = between-study variance; w_i* = RE weight
notes: The only difference from FE is the variance definition (p. 102). Spreadsheet K3 = I3 + J3, L3 = 1/K3. Carroll example: 1/(0.030 + 0.040) printed as 14.330, which uses unrounded tau^2 (1/0.070 would be 14.286) (p. 101). Engine: meta_analysis(model='random', tau2_method='DL').

name: Random-effects pooled estimate
variables: T_bar* = RE pooled estimate (estimated mean of the true-effect distribution); w_i* = RE weight; T_i = effect of study i

name: Variance and standard error of the RE pooled estimate
variables: v_bar* = variance of T_bar*; w_i* = RE weights; SE(T_bar*) = standard error
notes: Spreadsheet M14 = 1/L9, M15 = SQRT(M14). Example v_bar* = 0.0114, SE = 0.1068 (p. 101). This Wald SE is always >= the FE SE and equal only if tau^2 = 0 (p. 113). An HKSJ-rescaled SE (the engine's RE default) can be smaller when q < 1.

name: 95% Wald confidence interval and Z for the RE pooled estimate
variables: LL*, UL* = 95% limits; T_bar* = RE pooled estimate; SE(T_bar*) = its SE; Z* = test statistic; 1.96 = standard normal 0.975 quantile
notes: z-based (Wald) interval. Typo on p. 101: 'Upper Limit* = 0.3968 − 1.96*0.1068 = 0.5535' should read 0.3442 + 1.96*0.1068; the result 0.5535 is correct. Example CI 0.1350-0.5535, Z* = 3.2247. Engine default for model='random' is ci_method='hksj'; pass ci_method='z' to reproduce the source. [note: HKSJ/t-based intervals are generally preferred for RE when k is small.] The engine uses 1.959964 rather than 1.96 for ci_method='z'.

name: Relative weight (%) of a study
expression: RW_i = 100 * w_i / sum_{j=1..k}(w_j)   (FE: w_i = 1/v_i; RE: w_i* = 1/(v_i + tau^2))
variables: RW_i = relative weight of study i in percent; w_i = model-specific weight; k = number of studies
notes: Not printed as a formula; implied by the CMA 'Relative weight' columns (2 decimals). Engine returns it as MetaResult.weights_pct. Example: large study F 68% (FE) vs 23% (RE).

name: Variance of Cohen's d (inferred)
variables: d = standardized mean difference (Cohen's d); n1, n2 = group sample sizes; v_d = sampling variance of d; SE_d = its standard error
notes: NOT stated in this excerpt: inferred because it reproduces the printed SEs, variances and relative weights exactly with n1 = n2 = N/2. Engine: effect_sizes.smd(..., correct=False, vtype='LS') uses 1/n1 + 1/n2 + d^2/(2(n1+n2)), which is identical. effect_sizes.smd takes group means/SDs. To get v_d from a reported d and N (as in the CMA tables), evaluate the expression directly.
